primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: After prolonged starvation, rapid carbohydrate delivery raises insulin. Insulin drives phosphate and potassium into cells while anabolic pathways consume phosphate for phosphorylated intermediates and ATP. Depleted total-body stores make the fall in serum phosphate particularly dangerous, causing muscle weakness, respiratory failure, arrhythmias, and neurologic dysfunction.
vignette: A 24-year-old woman with severe anorexia nervosa is admitted after several weeks of minimal food intake. On admission, she is hemodynamically stable and has a low-normal serum phosphate concentration. Enteral nutrition is started. Two days later, she develops generalized weakness, shallow breathing, and frequent ventricular ectopy. Laboratory studies show marked hypophosphatemia, hypokalemia, and hypomagnesemia.
lead: Which of the following mechanisms most directly explains the new electrolyte abnormalities?
correct: A carbohydrate-induced rise in insulin drives phosphate and potassium into cells during renewed anabolic metabolism
distractors: Increased parathyroid hormone secretion causes renal phosphate wasting in response to acute hypercalcemia
Cell lysis releases intracellular phosphate and potassium into the extracellular fluid after nutritional therapy begins
Respiratory acidosis drives phosphate into cells while hydrogen ions move out of cells
Reduced proximal-tubule sodium-phosphate cotransporter expression from excess fibroblast growth factor 23 causes isolated renal phosphate wasting
distractor_notes: PTH-mediated phosphate wasting is not the defining event after refeeding and would not explain the simultaneous characteristic insulin-linked shifts in phosphate and potassium.
Cell lysis, as in tumor lysis syndrome, releases phosphate and potassium and therefore tends to raise rather than sharply lower their serum concentrations.
Respiratory acidosis is not the mechanism of the characteristic post-refeeding electrolyte pattern; the key trigger is insulin-driven intracellular uptake after carbohydrate delivery.
FGF23-mediated renal phosphate wasting can cause chronic hypophosphatemia but does not explain the abrupt multielectrolyte fall immediately after feeding a severely malnourished patient.
key_expl: Refeeding syndrome follows rapid nutritional replenishment after prolonged starvation. Rising glucose stimulates insulin, which drives phosphate and potassium intracellularly while anabolic metabolism increases phosphate utilization. Because total-body phosphate is already depleted, serum phosphate can fall precipitously, leading to ATP depletion, weakness, respiratory muscle dysfunction, and arrhythmias.
objective: Explain refeeding syndrome as an insulin-driven intracellular shift and utilization of phosphate and other electrolytes after carbohydrate reintroduction in a severely malnourished patient.
